To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) leisure activities are important predictors of initiation, progression and cessation of cannabis use; (b) the effects of different leisure activities on cannabis use are mediated through social network characteristics; (c) leisure activities are more important predictors of cannabis use among adolescents than among adults.

the following leisure time activities predict initiation, progression or reduction of cannabis use among adolescents: (a) playing sports; (b) going to the movies; (c) playing video games; and (d) watching TV.

the following activities were associated with an increased risk of cannabis initiation: (1) participation in sports and other physical activities, (2) participation in social clubs, (3) having a high number of friends, and (4) having a high level of social support.
